p2s.summary: The Results call the panel interval only "the panel's own 95% interval on 45.8%" and never say what interval it is; it is a nominal Wilson interval at n=190 that treats the 190 design records as independent draws, when they are 176 distinct molecules tiled 5 registers per junction across 38 junctions. The deposit's extended report calls the same quantity "nominal" and prints the clustering-corrected interval beside it; the journal article prints neither the word nor the corrected interval.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript at the pin, Results: "at ten the strongest null's 40.6% falls inside the panel's own 95% interval on 45.8%, as at every cut from seven to thirteen but eleven." research/modalities/aso-parent-null.json `_what_this_is_not[0]` at the pin: "The 190 design records are 176 distinct molecules tiled at overlapping registers across 38 junctions, so they are not independent draws and no test treating them as such would be right about its own denominator." `cut_sensitivity._why` in the same file calls it the "nominal Wilson interval". research/manuscripts/tests/test_clustered_intervals_are_computed_not_typed.py pins the extended report's clustered figures for this same rate (design effect, effective sample, interval). I recomputed both from research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json: one-way ANOVA over the 38 junctions at m=5 gives deff 1.422, effective sample 133.6 and a clustered Wilson interval of 37.6-54.2% against the nominal 38.9-52.9%; a 20,000-replicate cluster bootstrap over junctions gives [37.4%, 54.2%] and deff 1.40 (s27-statistics-cluster.txt, s27-statistics-clustered-ladder.txt). CHECKED, AND NOTHING MOVES: at every cut from 6 to 13 the strongest null falls inside the clustered interval at exactly the same cuts as the nominal one - inside at 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 and outside at 6 and 11 - so the sentence's "every cut from seven to thirteen but eleven" and its sole separation claim at eleven both survive the correction. This is a reporting gap, not a wrong result. A one-word fix that costs no length: "the panel's own nominal 95% interval on 45.8%".

p2s.summary: The pre-registered power figures rest on "an assumed replicate standard deviation of 0.35 on the natural-log scale" without saying that 0.35 is the standard deviation of the log RATIO. That is what the derivation uses, and it is what the paired design implies, but a laboratory reading it as the SD of each log half-maximal concentration would size the experiment against a materially different number.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript at the pin, Discussion: "At an assumed replicate standard deviation of 0.35 on the natural-log scale - also adopted for pre-registration, not measured - six independent biological replicates give about 80% power to falsify a true selectivity of 3 and three give about 30%." research/manuscripts/aso_falsification_power.py at the pin defines SIGMA = 0.35 and computes `ncp = (log_true - log_cut) * sqrt(n) / sigma` with df = n-1, i.e. a one-sample noncentral-t on the per-replicate log ratio. Executed at the pin (s27-statistics-power.txt): n=3 30.42%, n=6 81.28%, n=10 98.31%; void SDs 0.648, 1.534, 2.250 - all five printed figures reproduce, and the void figures reproduce only on a t interval with n-1 df, as the prose says. Sensitivity (s27-statistics-sigma-sensitivity.txt): if 0.35 were instead the SD of each log concentration and the two were independent, the ratio's SD is 0.495 and power at six replicates falls from 81.3% to 53.1% and at three from 30.4% to 18.7%. The paired reading is the right one - the paper says the ratio comes "from a matched dose-response in the same wells" and the void gate is stated on the interval of the ratio - so naming the quantity costs three words and removes the only place this design could be mis-sized.

p2s.summary: The Methods describe the ten-base-pair criterion as "a length of hybrid", immediately after quoting the enzyme's requirement in hybridised nucleotides. Every counted run contains exactly six RNA:DNA base pairs by construction; the rest are LNA:RNA wing pairs. The paper's own Results state this correctly four hundred words later, so the two sentences describe the same quantity in two units.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript at the pin, Introduction/Methods: "Its length requirement is reported as a DNA gap of at least six nucleotides, with seven to ten the working range; the screen below counts a liability only at ten contiguous base pairs of duplex through that gap, a length of hybrid rather than a count of gap nucleotides." Against the implementation, research/modalities/aso_parent_gap_pairing.py at the pin, the MIN_DUPLEX_BP comment: "NOT THE DNA GAP: a hit counts only if all six gap positions are paired, so the DNA:RNA run is 6 bp for EVERY counted hit by construction and this threshold does not test the catalytic DNA requirement at all", and its docstring: "exactly six of its ten to thirteen base pairs are the RNA:DNA gap, and the rest are LNA:RNA wing pairs that RNase-H1 does not cleave and its hybrid-binding domain does not recognise as hybrid". The manuscript already carries the right framing in Results - "These are whole-duplex run lengths rather than the enzyme's own unit" - which is why this holds nothing. A same-length fix: "a duplex length rather than a count of gap nucleotides".

p2s.summary: "At 5-10-5 pairing the whole gap already demands ten base pairs, more than the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to need" - ten is the top of the seven-to-ten range the same paper states, not more than it. The conclusion that follows (the 25.4% figure is a floor) is unaffected and correct.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript at the pin, Results, against its own Methods sentence "reported as a DNA gap of at least six nucleotides, with seven to ten the working range". The floor conclusion needs only ten >= seven, which holds; the overstatement is that the criterion is said to exceed even the strictest reading of the requirement when it equals it. The three geometry figures themselves reproduce from research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json at the pin: `n_at_or_above_min_duplex_bp` 87, 88, 87 over 190, 266 and 342 designs, i.e. 45.79%, 33.08% and 25.44% (s27-statistics-log.txt and the artifact's own `geometries` block).
